segment.description: Roaring River mainstem, rising on the Highland Rim near Livingston (Overton County) and flowing 37.7 miles to the Cordell Hull Lake confluence in Jackson County; includes the 20.5-mile Tennessee state scenic river reach.
segment.boundaries: TDEC scenic designation (April 4, 1968): Class I Natural River Area - 2 mi from State Route 136 downstream; Class II Pastoral River Area - approximately 18.5 mi from a point 2 mi downstream of SR 136 to the Cordell Hull Lake confluence. Upper Overton County headwater reaches above SR 136 are also part of the catalog water.

coldSource.notes: Elevation is the gage altitude (NAVD88) of USGS 03418000 Roaring River near Hilham, TN, from the NWIS site file. TDEC: the river originates on the Highland Rim near Livingston and flows 37.7 mi to Cordell Hull Lake; features include The Boils WMA (TWRA) and the USACE Roaring River Recreation Area at the confluence. The one impoundment on the reach - Tennessee's largest dam removal to date - was removed in 2018, reconnecting fish passage for warmwater natives (white bass, redhorse, Eastern hellbender).

holdover.detail: No trout stocking program exists for this river in TWRA data (TWRA's stocking schedule carries only Dale Hollow TW/Obey and Dale Hollow Reservoir in this area), and no holdover documentation was found.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documentation found in sources checked; agency and conservation descriptions of the river center on paddling, general fishing access, and warmwater native species, with no trout mention.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: TDEC, TWRA (Boils WMA), and the 2018 dam-removal record (white bass, redhorse, hellbender reconnection) all document a warmwater scenic river, and TWRA lists no trout stocking or trout regulation for it.

sourcesChecked: https://www.onwaterapp.com/us/tennessee/water/roaring-river-w1 (vendor trout claim, lead only - not cited)
